Header.CaseTitle: Heritage Brewing Company Ltd v Traditional Ales Holdings Plc
Header.AppealFrom: High Court of Justice, King's Bench Division

Counsel.Lead: Victoria Moore KC; David Roberts (instructed by Linklaters LLP)

SummaryOfPosition.Summary: The Respondent denies invalidity and contends that its mark was registered in good faith, that there is no likelihood of confusion, and that the Appellant's use is insufficient to found passing off rights.

FactsReliedOn.item: The Respondent's mark covers different goods and services from the Appellant's use.
The Appellant's use was geographically limited and did not establish national reputation.
The marks are sufficiently different to avoid likelihood of confusion.
The Respondent conducted searches before registration and did not discover the Appellant's use.
The Appellant delayed unreasonably in challenging the registration.

Contentions.item: The registration was made in good faith following proper searches.
There is no likelihood of confusion given the differences in marks and trade channels.
The Appellant lacks sufficient goodwill to maintain a passing off claim.
The challenge is out of time and should be dismissed.
